tagline: Desert kingdom of Petra and the Dead Sea
overview:
Jordan sits in the Middle East at the edge of the Arabian Desert, a country about the size of Indiana, bordered by Syria, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Israel and the West Bank. Its only stretch of coast is a short strip on the Gulf of Aqaba at the Red Sea, roughly 26 kilometers long, where coral reefs grow close to the beach. Amman, the capital, climbs across a cluster of steep hills and ranks among the longest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

About 11 million people live in Jordan, most of them Arabs, along with large communities of Palestinian and Syrian refugees who arrived over decades of regional conflict. Arabic is the official language, and English is widely taught. Jordan is a constitutional monarchy led by a king of the Hashemite family. With little oil and very little fresh water, the country relies on services, trade and tourism, and the ancient city of Petra draws visitors from around the world.
landAndNature: A line of hills runs down western Jordan and drops steeply into the Jordan Rift Valley, part of the same crack in the Earth's crust that continues through East Africa. At its lowest lies the Dead Sea, about 430 meters below sea level, the lowest land surface on the planet; its water is so salty that swimmers float without effort and no fish can survive in it. East of the hills spreads desert, including Wadi Rum, a valley of red sand and towering sandstone cliffs often used to film scenes set on Mars. Jordan is one of the driest countries on Earth, and ibex, striped hyenas and migrating birds cross its reserves.
peopleAndCulture: Mansaf is the national dish and the centerpiece of celebrations: lamb cooked in a sauce of dried fermented yogurt, spread over rice and flatbread and eaten from one shared platter. Falafel, hummus and thick cardamom coffee fill ordinary days. Bedouin traditions of hospitality run deep, and offering food and shelter to a traveler is a point of honor; many Bedouin families now live in towns, while some still keep goat-hair tents in the desert. Embroidery, mosaic-making and silver jewelry are traditional crafts. Soccer and basketball are popular, and Jordanian taekwondo athletes have won Olympic medals.
history: At Ain Ghazal near Amman, archaeologists found human statues about 9,000 years old, among the oldest ever made. The Nabataeans, desert traders, carved the city of Petra from rose-colored cliffs more than 2,000 years ago and controlled the incense routes until Rome absorbed their kingdom. Byzantine churches with detailed floor mosaics followed, then Islamic rule from the 600s, crusader castles, and four centuries within the Ottoman Empire. After World War I Britain administered the area, and the Emirate of Transjordan gained full independence in 1946 as the Kingdom of Jordan. Jordan took part in the Arab-Israeli wars, governed the West Bank from 1950 until 1967, and signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994.
funFacts: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest dry land on Earth, about 430 meters below sea level.
Petra holds roughly 800 monuments carved straight into sandstone cliffs, including the famous facade called the Treasury.
The Dead Sea is so salty that people float on the surface and cannot easily sink beneath it.
The red desert of Wadi Rum has stood in for the surface of Mars in several films.
Jordan is one of the most water-scarce countries in the world, and many homes keep water in rooftop tanks.
